articles.title: Everything new coming to Meta’s AI agent Muse
articles.summary: CEO Mark Zuckerberg kicked off the company’s annual Connect event in Menlo Park on Wednesday with a keynote that made one thing clear: Meta is going all-in on Muse. It's even coming to Meta's AI glasses.

articles.title: Meta made a Tamagotchi-like wearable for its Muse AI agent
articles.summary: The tiny hardware device creates another mobile home for its AI agent Muse.

articles.title: Meta is making a standalone Muse AI gadget
articles.summary: Meta is building a dedicated hardware device for its new Muse AI agent. The product, called Muse Charm, was briefly shown off by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg at the end of tonight's Meta Connect presentation.

articles.title: Meta introduces camera-free AI glasses
articles.summary: Meta says the camera-free glasses will be lighter and have up to 12 hours battery life.

articles.title: Meta ditches the camera on its newest smart glasses
articles.summary:
The Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses have no cameras. | Photo by Brett Putman / The Verge
Walking around Meta Connect 2026, everyone's sporting smart glasses in all sorts of shapes, colors, and sizes.

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026: The biggest news and announcements
articles.summary: It’s about time for Meta Connect, the company’s annual product launch event. This year, given the company’s major focus on AI and wearables like smart glasses, it seems likely that we’ll see updates from CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his team on those categories.

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026 live blog: On the ground at Mark Zuckerberg’s next big product launch
articles.summary:
It's time once again for Meta's annual September product launch event, and
The Verge
is on the ground in Menlo Park to cover the show live. Meta
says that
today's keynote by Mark Zuckerberg will be about how "Meta is building a future for everyone" - something he wrote at length about
in a recent essay
about AI, smart glasses, and more.

articles.title: Anthropic says its biology lab has already found something big
articles.summary: But maybe the biggest reveal is that Anthropic has not let Claude run loose in its biology lab. Humans are still, so far, in the loop.

articles.title: Enveda secures $311M to bring more nature-derived AI drugs into clinical trials
articles.summary: The round valued the AI biotech at $2 billion. It is currently testing drugs that treat skin conditions and preserve weight loss after stopping GLP-1s.

articles.title: Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
articles.summary:
It never ceases to amaze me how I can be doing
nothing at all
, minding my own business, and suddenly something needs to be taken care of. You're telling me a tree branch fell in the backyard and now I have to figure out what to do with it?

articles.title: Data centers are black boxes, but California wants to change that
articles.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a slate of bills on Monday that could finally give communities better data - and more say - on how data centers impact their electricity bills and water supply. As data centers invade a growing number of communities across the US, they've triggered protests over how the infrastructure underpinning AI might stress power…

articles.title: Anthropic’s biolab made a discovery it’s comparing to Crispr
articles.summary:
Anthropic says its AI Claude has "autonomously discovered" a new enzyme system similar to machinery behind the powerful gene-editing tool Crispr. It's the first result from Anthropic's
newly-launched wet lab
and an early test of Claude's usefulness for science as the company prepares to go public.

articles.title: ChatGPT mobile app gets voice-based agentic features
articles.summary: Pro and Plus users will be able to use the Work tab on their phones to complete agentic tasks.

articles.title: Even Americans who use AI every day are worried about it
articles.summary: The report suggests that greater exposure will not resolve the unease around the technology, nor reduce public support for AI regulation.

articles.title: Bernie Sanders proposes banning ‘superintelligence’ and putting violators in prison
articles.summary:
Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX)
have introduced new legislation
that would ban anyone from developing artificial superintelligence - a technology the bill describes as capable of the "destruction or disempowerment of humanity," including by overthrowing the government. Under the
Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act

articles.title: YouTube Music gets more conversational with new AI features
articles.summary: Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists.

articles.title: YouTube is building AI creator tools that do almost everything for them
articles.summary:
At the annual creator-focused Made on YouTube event, the company announced updates to the suite of AI-powered creator tools it
unveiled in 2025
. In its initial iteration, the dashboard of creator tools included things like A/B testing for video thumbnails and a chatbot interface to query how content was performing.

articles.title: YouTube releases new AI features for creators within its Studio app
articles.summary: YouTube is adding new features to generate ideas and monitor the performance of thumbnails.

articles.title: YouTube will let you build your own algorithm with AI
articles.summary: YouTube’s new custom feeds let users describe the videos they want to see in their own words, then use Gemini to build a personalized feed around the request.

Patreon cofounder Sam Yam is joining OpenAI to lead Creator Product. | Image: The Verge

articles.summary: Most leaders on a trade mission stick to the pitch, but when I interviewed Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis this week, he also admitted that no government is ready for what AI is about to do.

articles.summary:
On Monday, the company
announced
a new independent panel of mathematicians tasked with advising it and other AI companies on their interactions with mathematical research and the wider mathematics community, including how new results are presented and released. Its abrupt arrival caught many mathematicians by surprise.

articles.title: Rabbit’s new AI agent doesn’t need an R1 to run
articles.summary: According to Rabbit, you can add up to five devices to one account, along with your preferred AI models. OS3 will automatically determine the devices, files, apps, and AI models it needs to complete a task.

articles.summary: Meta says Muse was built from scratch, but acknowledges the AI assistant was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw — down to some of its workspace filenames and content.

Anthropic says its new Claude Opus 5.5 model comes with stronger safeguards in the wake of recent rogue AI hacking incidents. In

articles.title: She died at the San Diego border. A surveillance camera was in plain sight

articles.summary: The first is that we barely understand how AI works, and it’s quickly growing more powerful. There is lots of ongoing research about how to monitor and control misbehaving agents, but the current approaches are fragile.
